summary: Announcements can now be posted into a group chat timeline behind the new default-OFF flag chat_announcements (registered, seeded off, exposed as features.chat_announcements). Design: one announcement record, one optional server-generated messages line (system_kind='announcement', announcement_id link, constant text 'posted an announcement'), persisted directly like the pin line (no chat push, announcement push stays the only one). New files: api/backend/interactions/chat_announcements.py (all logic) and api/schema_ddl/chat_announcements.py (registered in db.py DDL_MODULES): group_announcements.post_to_chat BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE (author opt-in, no backfill), messages.announcement_id UUID FK ON DELETE CASCADE, unique partial index (exactly one line per announcement), partial due index. Thin hook-ins only: routes/group_announcements.py (post_to_chat StrictBool on create, 422 while flag off; background emit; sync frames on edit/delete/restore), announcements.py (post_to_chat param + one mark call inside the create transaction), groups.py (_system_filter + two attach calls + system_kind passthrough + announcement_id added to internal columns), scheduler.py (60s fire_due_chat_announcements job, 1h lookback so nothing is backfilled and reminders/repeats never emit), flags.py/schema_ddl/flags.py. api/main.py untouched. Read side is derived, not copied: history hides lines when the flag is off for the viewer or the announcement is deleted/unpublished, so delete/restore/edit need no row rewrites and cannot drift; blocked/departed authors are excluded by the existing author_set; each viewer gets their own serialized announcement plus 'edited' (updated_at > created_at + 5s) on both legacy and paged history; a line whose announcement can't load is dropped, never a placeholder. Live frames (flag-on members only): normal message frame + announcement_id + viewer-neutral announcement card, and {type: announcement_updated, action: updated|deleted|restored}. Auth unchanged and deny-by-default: _open membership 403, check_limit 'announcements' still enforced (verified 403 with post_to_chat), content filter unchanged; poster must still be a live member and flag-on at emit time. Docs updated: api/schema_tree.md, docs/architecture/backend.md (section + scheduler row), docs/api/overview.md. Verified with a throwaway smoke script against a private scratch Postgres (not committed, no repo tests written; testing gate owns tests): DDL twice, flag-off 422, limit, emit once + idempotent, live frame, history payload, edit/edited, delete hides, restore shows, sync frames, non-member 403, blocked author hidden, flag-off viewer sees nothing, scheduled emit on due tick, stale scheduled not emitted, cascade. Existing suites still pass on that scratch DB: test_group_announcements 121, polls 96, push 61, repeat 224, attachments 74, location/style/title_color, chat_pagination 265, chat_pagination_endpoints 153 (test_member_joined_line and test_message_pins could not be run because they hard-assert port 55432, which was occupied by another session's cluster). Notes for later gates: (1) 20261020-announcement-title-position-size is NOT in this worktree's api (no title_position); the line's announcement dict is whatever AnnouncementsManager._serialize emits, so title styling lands automatically when that merges. (2) Frontend should treat the frame card as neutral and re-GET the announcement for can_edit/RSVP/poll/flag-gated fields; create body field is post_to_chat. (3) Security gate: attach_announcements opens one extra AnnouncementsManager connection per history page that contains announcement lines (only when flag on and lines present). (4) Tracked __pycache__ .pyc files were restored after test runs; no push, deploy or production migration performed.
